subject: brain
angle: While specific brain regions are lateralized for functions like language and spatial attention, there is no evidence for a global "left-brained" or "right-brained" phenotype across individuals.
title: The Myth of Hemispheric Dominance

hooks.text: Are you really only using half of your brain?
You believe in two hemispheres. The data see local networks.
You are using a myth to simplify your own identity.
A steady hand over a keyboard.

reveal.headline: There is no global left-brained or right-brained phenotype.
reveal.body: Data do not support a whole-brain phenotype of greater strength in one hemisphere over another across individuals.

explain.headline: Lateralization is a local property.
explain.body: Specific brain regions are lateralized for tasks like language or spatial attention. However, these are local features of brain networks, not a global characteristic of your brain.

matters.headline: Your brain is not a binary.
matters.body: That may be why you do not fit into a single category of personality. Your brain functions through localized networks rather than a total hemispheric split.

example.headline: A split screen on a monitor.
example.body: You watch a video while typing a message. Your brain manages these tasks through specific networks, not by switching between two different sides of your head.

question.headline: Which label have you been using to define your own mind?

verdict: The evidence shows that while specific tasks and conditions (like handedness or neurodevelopmental disorders) influence hemispheric asymmetry, there is no evidence for a whole-brain phenotype of greater left or right-brain strength.
caveat: The studies show that lateralization is often a local property of brain networks rather than a global characteristic.
caption:
The idea of being left-brained or right-brained is a myth.

Research shows no evidence for a whole-brain phenotype of greater strength in one hemisphere. Lateralization is a local property of brain networks rather than a global characteristic. 

How does this change how you view your own cognitive style?
